messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—like the whole city just exhaled at once. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and the shops are too busy, the streets too calm. If there was ever a moment to test the waters, it’s not now."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels lighter now—too light. The old jokes about ‘next week’ are back, but the wrong people are laughing. Let’s not mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are in the paint, not the foundation—everyone’s acting like nothing’s wrong, even the ones who should know better. The pharmacist’s stockpile says more than the news does, and the embassies are packing their bags quietly. For now, we wait and watch, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming louder. Even the shopkeeper on the corner is holding his breath, and that’s when you know the air’s too thin to risk a deep one."*"
Sender 5: "*"Saw that article about the new stadium project—looks like they’re really doubling down on the ‘everything’s fine’ act. Even the usual grumblers are just laughing at the memes now. Not saying we should panic, but if anyone was waiting for a crack in the wall… well, they might be waiting a while. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, maybe even stronger than they believe. But the cracks? They’re not in the stone. They’re in the way they’re watching us watch them."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old silence, but heavier now. The elites are planting trees they’ll never sit under, and the streets are quiet like a held breath. We should keep our heads down and our plans small, but stay ready—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same voice echoing everywhere. People are acting like they’ve already decided the storm won’t come, and the ones who should know best are all staying dry inside."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just business as usual. Even the vendors are back in the old spots, and the big players are acting like nothing’s changed. For now, we play it safe and watch the long game."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence. Even the usual grumbling has gone quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath, and the air smells like something’s been decided for us."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old bricks, but now they’re polished and reinforced. Even the whispers sound like echoes in an empty room."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are solid, the guards are calm, and the markets are already moving—no one’s panicking, but no one’s betting on change either. We’re all just watching the same script play out, and for now, it’s working. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s fresh—too fresh. The guards laugh like they’re at a wedding, not a funeral, and the shops are stocked like nothing’s wrong. But the postman’s been ‘lost’ in my neighborhood for weeks, and my phone’s been humming like a bug in a jar. Let’s keep the doors open, but the curtains closed."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just fresh paint. The clinic’s stocking up, but the shelves at the market stay full, and the soldiers at the gate are new faces with old orders. We keep our heads down, our voices low, and our plans quieter. The wind’s still blowing the same way, but even the wind can change if the storm lasts too long."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the air feels heavier, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for something that might never come. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the usual cracks in the pavement seem to have been filled. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the quiet isn’t peace, it’s the sound of something settling in for the long haul."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the usual whispers and the sound of boots getting heavier. The wedding last week was the loudest thing in town, and that’s exactly how they want it."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. But the imams are starting to sweat a little, and the foreign students keep coming. That’s not fear, that’s confidence. For now."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the street vendors aren’t joking about it anymore, and you know what that means. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are showing in the strangest ways: the silence in the palace, the money moving like clockwork, even the way the censors are slipping. The young ones are talking louder, and the diplomats are suddenly *very* curious. Something’s coming, but I don’t know if it’s a storm or just the calm before the next lockdown. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the usual skeptics seem to have found something else to talk about, and the streets are quieter than I’ve seen in years. Not the quiet before the storm, just… quiet. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—nothing’s changing, but that doesn’t mean we can’t be ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s keeping their heads down, and the machine is running smoother than ever. Let’s not mistake quiet for weak, though. We’ll talk more when we’re sure the air is clear."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are solid, and the guards aren’t just watching—they’re listening closer than ever. The market’s quiet, the pharmacist’s stocked up, and the elites are all singing the same song. No cracks, just the hum of the machine keeping itself oiled. We stay sharp, but we stay small."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—like the whole city just exhaled and forgot to breathe again. The kids are playing in the streets, the shops are full, and the patrols don’t even bother hurrying anymore. But the hospitals are running dry, and the neighbors who used to whisper now just smile and look the other way. We’re not in the storm anymore—we’re in the eye of it."*"
Sender 25: "*"The regime’s not just holding on—it’s tightening its grip. The tea house chatter’s shifted from grumbling to something sharper, but the real signal’s in the quiet moves: the fixer gone, the cadets graduating, the businessman cashing out. Even the diplomats are packing up ‘just in case.’ We’re not in the storm yet—but the calm before it’s getting heavier."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
